blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Nathan announces that David's offspring will build the temple and that the LORD will establish his throne, and David answers in prayer. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

For a later or comparative connection, note that Second Samuel 7 promises an enduring Davidic house, includes father-son relationship and discipline for wrongdoing, and withholds temple building from David; later texts develop how enduring promise and historical judgment relate. This remains a secondary connection rather than the chapter's first-audience context. It can be traced further without replacing the chapter's own setting. Interpretations differ on some details.
